title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Quiet weekend, no new U.S. trading since Friday's close. Recap: Nasdaq led stocks higher (+1.2%), S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow +0.5% (~250 pts) after a much-weaker-than-expected September jobs report (+29,000 jobs, unemployment up to 4.2%) eased fears the Fed would reverse its rate-cut path.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield ended Friday near 5.3%, just below this week's 24-year high; French yields stayed elevated amid the country's fiscal standoff, with France's 2-year near 2008-era levels.

Markets: Crude oil fell 1.9% Friday to $91.11/bbl after the G-7 agreed to jointly release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves to ease the global diesel crunch tied to the Ukraine and Middle East wars.

Companies: Anthropic and OpenAI remain locked in an IPO race — Anthropic filed first and could list as early as this fall, while OpenAI has confidentially filed too, targeting 2027 but open to moving sooner.
Companies: No major weekend corporate headlines; next week brings earnings from PepsiCo and Delta Air Lines, plus U.S. services PMI and FOMC meeting minutes.
Macro/Policy: France's Lecornu government remains under pressure over its 2027 budget (~€54B in cuts) ahead of a Nov. 17 confidence vote, following Scope Ratings' downgrade to A+.
Macro/Policy: U.S. government shutdown risk has receded for now — Congress funded federal agencies through Dec. 11, pushing the next funding fight past the midterm elections.
